data.executive_summary: This report evaluates a heart disease risk classification task using medical features. The Random Forest model achieved 77.8% accuracy with an AUC of 0.85, identifying age, heart rate, and ST depression as key predictors. The model correctly classified 74% of actual cases but had a 26% error rate overall.
data.methodology: We used Random Forest Classifier for binary classification of heart disease risk. The model was trained on medical features including age, blood pressure, cholesterol, and ECG measurements. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 metrics. Visualizations included actual vs predicted scatter plots and residual distribution histograms.
data.results_analysis: The model achieved 77.8% accuracy (0.7778) with precision, recall, and F1 all at 0.77-0.78. Prediction statistics showed a mean of 0.6087 with 49.34% standard deviation across 46 samples. Visualizations revealed MAE of 0.2222 and RMSE of 0.4714. The model demonstrated better sensitivity (77.8%) than specificity, with 12/46 incorrect predictions (26% error rate).
data.conclusions: The Random Forest model successfully predicted heart disease risk with 77.8% accuracy, identifying key medical features as important predictors. While the model shows reasonable performance, the 26% error rate indicates room for improvement through feature engineering and class balance optimization.
data.recommendations:
1. Test with SMOTE to address potential class imbalance
2. Explore feature interactions between age and heart rate metrics
3. Validate model performance on external datasets
4. Consider adding clinical features like family history
5. Perform hyperparameter tuning for optimal performance
